science.title: Integrative meta-transcriptomics and machine learning reveal defence networks and regulatory hubs in response to tomato bacterial pathogens
science.description: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is an economically important vegetable crop, however, its production is severely affected by bacterial pathogens, including Clavibacter michiganensis subsp. michiganensis (Cmm) and Pseudomonas syringae. Plant defence responses are regulated by complex hormonal networks, particularly salicylic acid and jasmonic acid, which activate partially overlapping and context-dependent signalling pathways. Although numerous transcriptomic studies have investigated hormone- and pathogen-associated responses, conserved transcriptional signatures underlying tomato defence remain incompletely understood. To address this, we performed an integrative meta-analysis of massive RNA-seq data using five complementary approaches (fixed-effects, random-effects, Rank Product, Stouffer’s Z-score, and Fisher’s method), identifying 178 upregulated and 177 downregulated consensus DEGs representing a core hormone-responsive signature. Functional enrichment analysis revealed extensive metabolic and regulatory reprogramming involving amino acid metabolism, lipid-associated processes, vesicle trafficking, redox regulation and defence-associated signalling pathways. Protein-protein interaction analysis highlighted highly connected genes, including P5CS (Solyc08G000796) and glutathione reductase (Solyc09G002031), which were associated with proline metabolism and redox homeostasis. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) combined with machine learning-based feature selection enabled the prioritization of integrative candidate genes, including a xyloglucan endotransglucosylase/hydrolase (Solyc09G000233) and other poorly characterized candidates. In addition, the Random Forest model independently prioritized several highly important features, including Solyc10G001545, Solyc10G002708, Solyc07G002639, Solyc12G001296 which showed strong associations with defence-related transcriptional variation. Collectively, our findings suggest that tomato defence responses involve a complex regulatory landscape integrating metabolic adjustment, signaling processes, redox balance, and cell wall-associated responses. The combination of transcriptomic meta-analysis, network biology, and machine learning provides a framework for prioritizing candidate genes and generating hypotheses for future functional studies aimed at understanding tomato defence responses.
